results.content: Every September and October before a midterm, the same question resurfaces in polling coverage: could the polls be wrong? This time, there’s a follow up: are Democrats leading by too much? A Change Research national survey of 2,021 registered voters, conducted September 15-24, 2026, illustrates why the challenge inherent in that question. Democrats lead the 2026 congressional generic ballot by 7 points overall. ## The Tilt

The map favors Republicans, but cracks in their base are leaving them vulnerable in defending House and Senate control.

The final New York Times/Siena University national poll of the 2026 midterm campaign finds Democrats leading nationally by 11 percentage points, 52 to 41 percent, when likely voters were asked about the specific candidates for the House in their district.
results.title: Democrats Have a Wide Lead in Our New Poll as Trump Slides - The New York Times

results.content:

In September, the Democrats had a 12-point advantage on the generic congressional ballot question among registered voters.

results.content:
In Silver’s midterm election forecast model, the generic ballot gives Democrats a 51.3–41.6 lead over Republicans, a 9.6-point margin (9.1 points in my September 25 article). Democrats’ lead had dropped to 7.4 points on September 4.

Polls that screen for likely voters usually give Democrats larger leads than polls that ask registered voters. Democrats are more likely to vote at lower turnout elections like the midterms than Republicans, when Trump is not on the ballot. [...] As I previously wrote, owing to Republican gerrymandering, Democrats need at least a four-point margin in the generic ballot to have a good chance to win the House majority.
